title: Release of Environmental Impact Assessment Report for Cross Island MRT Line
what_it_is: Release of Environmental Impact Assessment Report for Cross Island MRT Line

sections.label: EIA phases and alignment options
sections.summary: Phase 1 of the EIA focuses on site investigation impact on two alignment options, with findings needed for Phase 2's detailed assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Phase 1 of the EIA, which is where we are right now, focuses on the impact of site investigation on the two alignment options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The data and the findings from the site investigation are needed for Phase 2 of the EIA, which will provide a detailed assessment of the environmental impact of the construction and the operations of the CRL based on those two possible alignments.

sections.label: Reducing boreholes to protect forest
sections.summary: Boreholes will be cut from 72 to 16 and confined to existing trails to avoid affecting vegetation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To minimise these disturbances and damage to the forest environment, the number of boreholes to be drilled will be reduced from an earlier estimate of 72 down to 16.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: More importantly, these boreholes will be confined to existing trails so as not to affect any vegetation.

sections.label: Publishing EIA information and consultation
sections.summary: Questions were asked on releasing future EIAs online and publishing decision information, with the reply that Phase 1 is still ongoing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will the Government, as a default position, be releasing future EIAs that are done in relation to other projects online, as the default stance of the Government?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The second question is in relation to the on-going studies that are going to be done over the next two years, as the Senior Minister of State mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is early days yet, but my question is: will the Government consider publishing all the information that is relevant to making this decision and evaluating the trade-offs, in a single document and releasing that document for public debate and public consultation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As for the second question by the hon Member, we are still at Phase 1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Let us work through Phase 1, consider people's views, focus on what needs to be done for the soil investigation and, in tandem with the Ministry of Transport and LTA, let us consider the Member's suggestions as to what level of information would be useful for members of the public and interested persons to consider.
